🛡️ Wildlife & Alpine Environmental Safety Protocols

Mandatory precautions for Rocky Mountain grizzly habitat, sub-zero alpine passes, and remote boreal corridors
🐻 Grizzly & Black Bear Safety Protocol
  • Bear Spray Mounting: Keep 1 canister holstered on rider body or handlebar ram-mount. Never pack inside locked panniers.
  • Clean Bike Rule: Wipe down tank bags and saddles after eating trail mix or snacks. Store all food in bear-proof lockers or hotel rooms overnight.
  • Wildlife Sightings: Maintain 100m distance from bears and 30m from elk/moose. Never dismount running bikes in wildlife jams.
❄️ Mountain Pass Hypothermia & Rain Defense
  • Sunwapta Pass & Bow Summit (2,088m): Ambient temperatures drop 6.5°C per 1,000m gain. Snow flurries occur even in July.
  • Heated Gear Deployment: Power heated jacket liners from Africa Twin & Multistrada auxiliary DIN ports before ascending.
  • Emergency Rain Layer: Don Gore-Tex oversuits at first raindrop before thermal sweat creates hypothermia risk at speed.
🦌 Northern Highway 11 Moose Collision Hazards
  • Zero Dusk/Dawn Riding: Conclude all stages before 17:30 to avoid dusk moose feeding activity along swamp ditches.
  • Longlac to Hearst (194 km Gap): Pure wilderness corridor with zero cellular coverage. Operate Garmin inReach satellite tracking.
  • Brake Cushion: Ride staggered formation with 3-second spacing to allow sudden heavy braking for darting wildlife.
